maya: Morning — taking primary for the next 8h (local TZ). Omar will be secondary. Quick summary of gaps and playbook pointers below — please read if you're covering any pages. :wave:

omar: ack, I'll be on-call and available for escalations. tagging in the GPU infra folks for the 02:00–04:00 PST window gap.

jin: FYI we still have a flaky tail-latency alert for dedicated-gpu-prod (high p99 tokens). link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/latency/dedicated?var=service=gpu-proxy

maya: thanks @jin — if that fires while I'm primary, follow this quick triage checklist (TL;DR first, full runbooks below):
- TL;DR: check fleet health, restart model-proxy on affected nodes, verify KV-cache hit-rate, fallback to smaller model variant. :arrow_right:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/latency-triage
- GPU fleet checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-fleet-ops

maya: Quick commands to run from support jumpbox:```bash
# list pods with high cpu/oom
kubectl -n inference top pods | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10
# restart proxy on a node (replace <pod>)
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-proxy --field-selector metadata.name=<pod>
# tail proxy logs
kubectl -n inference logs -f deploy/model-proxy -c proxy --tail=200
```

omar: if restart doesn't help, scale a canary to take traffic:```bash
kubectl -n inference scale deploy model-proxy-canary --replicas=5
# update routing weight
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" https://router.redwood.local/traffic -d '{"service":"model-proxy","weight":0.2}'
```

ellie: I'll handle PagerDuty escalation updates — there's a small coverage gap 02:00–04:00 PST where no GPU infra owner is in rotation. I'll shift an on-call from platform for that window.

maya: coverage notes: 1) No hardware on-call 02:00–04:00 PST (gap) 2) Night ops (EMEA) only covers api-gateway, not dedicated GPU pool. If a page hits outside normal windows, escalate to platform@redwood and ping `#eng-oncall` immediately.

jin: Customer-impact checklist: always set incident severity in PagerDuty, add customer tags (`redwood:dedicated-cust-42`) and capture ETA for mitigation. Sample blurb for customer updates: 
> We're investigating elevated generation latency for Dedicated customers on the GPU pool. We've initiated restarts and are routing a portion of traffic to a fallback model to reduce latency. Next update in 15 minutes.

maya: quick remediation order of ops (short):
1) Check grafana alerts + routing queue length.
2) Verify node GPU memory and KV cache hit-rate.
3) Restart proxy on 1 node, monitor.
4) Canary scale + route 10–20% traffic to canary.
5) If continues, failover heavy customers to smaller model variant (policy: `fallback:small`), notify sales/CS.

ryan: I'll cover the 02:00–03:00 PST slice if ellie needs help. Also: if you need a blunt emergency mitigation, flip `router.force_fallback=true` in staging then prod with a canary first. Command: `POST /admin/force_fallback` with reason.

sre-shift-bot: Reminder — check the oncall checklist at shift start: https://confluence.redwood.ai/oncall/checklist. Last runbook audit was 2025-05-12; flag any stale links here.

maya: small runbook TL;DR for quick copy/paste (for pings):
- Latency triage: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/latency-triage (steps 1–6)
- GPU fleet ops: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-fleet-ops (hardware & driver recovery)
- Routing fallback: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/routing-fallback (how to change traffic weights and force fallback)

omar: noted. I'll take first pages for the next hour while maya finishes some docs. If you page me and I'm slow, escalate to ryan -> ellie.

maya: final notes: update the incident thread with exact commands you ran, CTRL-C logs into the ticket, and mark `mitigation` steps in the runbook. If anyone is short on coverage, ping me and I'll reassign. :memo:
